title: Color, Backgrounds, and Typography
summary: Build readable visual hierarchy with foreground and background colors, font families, type scale, weight, line height, and alignment.

sketchBlocks.title: Foreground and background colors establish contrast and grouping
Font family, size, and weight make importance visible
Line height and alignment affect readability

quizDraft.title: Choose the text-color property
quizDraft.hint: Think about which declaration changes the visible text itself rather than the area behind it.

help.concept: CSS has separate declarations for the appearance of text and for the surface behind an element.
help.hint_1: Focus on the declaration that affects the letters you read.
help.hint_2: Choose the option that changes the visible text without changing the surrounding surface.

quizDraft.title: Choose site-wide typography and readability decisions
quizDraft.prompt: Which CSS decisions support a consistent, readable visual system across the portfolio? Select all that apply.
quizDraft.hint: Look for choices that create reusable defaults or improve text rhythm without forcing content into arbitrary dimensions.

help.concept: Good typography combines shared defaults with readable spacing while remaining flexible for real content.
help.hint_1: Site-wide defaults belong on a broad shared ancestor; line height controls spacing between lines.
help.hint_2: Duplicated inline presentation and fixed text heights work against reuse and flexible content.

options: Use body for broad foreground, background, and font defaults that can be shared by the page.
Use line-height on paragraphs to improve vertical reading rhythm without changing the text.
Give every h2 a separate inline color so each page owns an unrelated heading style.
Force paragraphs to a fixed height so all text blocks occupy exactly the same vertical space.

quizDraft.title: Identify typography controls
quizDraft.prompt: Which properties can directly contribute to a text hierarchy?
quizDraft.hint: Choose CSS properties that affect the visual treatment of text.

help.concept: Size, weight, and family are typography controls.
help.hint_1: Choose CSS properties that affect the visual treatment of text.
help.hint_2: Select every choice that matches the lesson, not just one.

quizDraft.title: Order a basic typography plan
quizDraft.prompt: Arrange these decisions from broad defaults to targeted emphasis.
quizDraft.hint: Start with page-wide defaults before heading emphasis.

help.concept: A consistent typography system begins with defaults and adds deliberate hierarchy.
help.hint_1: Start with page-wide defaults before heading emphasis.
help.hint_2: Follow the sequence from targeting an element to seeing the browser render it.

quizDraft.title: Name the reading-rhythm property
quizDraft.prompt: Choose the property that controls spacing between lines of text.
quizDraft.hint: Think about the declaration that controls vertical breathing room between lines of text.

help.concept: Readable typography depends not only on typeface and size but also on the vertical rhythm between lines.
help.hint_1: This setting affects spacing from one line of text to the next.
help.hint_2: Choose the typography property concerned with vertical line spacing, not font size or alignment.

quizDraft.template: [blank1] controls the vertical distance between lines within text.

quizDraft.title: Choose the typography control
quizDraft.prompt: Complete the statement about emphasizing text with CSS.
quizDraft.hint: Think about the typography setting that changes how heavy the letter strokes appear.

help.concept: Typography includes independent controls for typeface, size, emphasis, spacing, and alignment.
help.hint_1: This setting changes visual emphasis without changing the text content.
help.hint_2: Choose the property concerned with stroke heaviness rather than size, spacing, or alignment.

quizDraft.template: To control how bold text appears, use the [blank1] property.

quizDraft.title: Establish a site-wide color and type foundation
quizDraft.prompt:
## CSS task

The site has a few accent rules now, but the page canvas and typography still feel like browser defaults. A body rule establishes broad inherited `color` and font choices from one site-wide foundation. Continue the existing stylesheet. Add a `body` rule with `background-color: #f8fafc`, `color: #1e293b`, and `font-family: Arial, sans-serif`. Preview more than one page. Compare several pages: the canvas should become softly tinted, default text should darken, and the typography should use the same sans-serif family.

### File to edit

`styles.css`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on.
quizDraft.hint: Use one body rule for the site-wide `background`, foreground, and font foundation.

help.concept: A body rule establishes broad inherited `color` and font choices from one site-wide foundation.
help.hint_1: Use one body rule for the site-wide `background`, foreground, and font foundation.
help.hint_2: Compare several pages: the canvas should become softly tinted, default text should darken, and the typography should use the same sans-serif family.

quizDraft.title: Give section headings a stronger foreground color
quizDraft.prompt:
## CSS task

Body copy is clearer, but section headings do not yet stand apart strongly enough from the surrounding text. A dedicated h2 foreground `color` creates a consistent hierarchy across every page that uses section headings. Keep all previous styles. Add `h2 { color: #0f172a; }` so section headings across the multi-page portfolio share a stronger foreground `color`. Preview About, Projects, and Contact: h2 headings should read darker and more authoritative than paragraph text.

### File to edit

`styles.css`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on.
quizDraft.hint: Use the shared h2 element type rather than page-specific selectors.

help.concept: A dedicated h2 foreground `color` creates a consistent hierarchy across every page that uses section headings.
help.hint_1: Use the shared h2 element type rather than page-specific selectors.
help.hint_2: Preview About, Projects, and Contact: h2 headings should read darker and more authoritative than paragraph text.

quizDraft.title: Improve paragraph readability
quizDraft.prompt:
## CSS task

The colors are working, but longer paragraphs still feel vertically cramped. Line `height` adds breathing room between lines without changing the content or creating artificial margins between paragraphs. Keep the cumulative stylesheet and add `line-height: 1.6;` to the existing `p` rule. Preview text-heavy sections on About and Projects as well as Home. Read a text-heavy section in the preview: paragraphs should feel easier to scan while their `color` and `width` stay the same.

### File to edit

`styles.css`

### Check your work

Keep the site's existing cumulative work, make the requested change, then compare the **Preview** with the **Expected result** before moving on.
quizDraft.hint: Extend the existing paragraph styling rather than replacing it.

help.concept: Line `height` adds breathing room between lines without changing the content or creating artificial margins between paragraphs.
help.hint_1: Extend the existing paragraph styling rather than replacing it.
help.hint_2: Read a text-heavy section in the preview: paragraphs should feel easier to scan while their `color` and `width` stay the same.
